executive_assessment.text: Territorial rainfall and rural livelihood evidence is complemented by named pilot watersheds and eight districts' participatory water-governance activities; these are selected examples, not complete local risk rankings.

The retrospective Dniester pollution account identifies Cosăuți abstraction, Soroca and Bălți service effects and differentiated access difficulties. It concerns a war-related shock, not climate attribution or verified current outages.

Reported plans, procurement, training and proposed cross-border protocols are capacities or intended measures, not proven resilience or peace effects. No complete supported climate-FCV chain is assembled.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated not stated reports: FAO describes the south as hot and arid, with 5-6 droughts per decade; about 75% of Moldova is dry, subhumid or semiarid land.
Source dated not stated reports: FAO lists a 2019 National Drought Plan, local emergency commissions' five-year preparedness plans and water-hazard warning and response protocols.
Source dated not stated reports: An active 2024-2027 project covers five named watersheds and targets flood early warning, dam safety and local integrated water-resources governance.
Source dated not stated reports: UNDP reports procurement of 10 hydrometeorological stations for five pilot areas and ground-penetrating radar for national dam monitoring.
Source dated not stated reports: Local action groups involve residents of eight districts, particularly women and vulnerable groups, in flood plans, dam priorities and protective measures.
Source dated not stated reports: UNDP reports training 35 specialists in digital climate-event modelling, 60 in dam flood-safety, and 50 in water-structure operation and assessment.
Source dated 2026-10-16 reports: Older, disabled, low-income and transport-limited people faced added difficulty; Soroca was most affected and Bălți moved classes online.
Source dated 2026-10-16 reports: Authorities, partners and businesses distributed over 620 tonnes of water; emergency medical services continued while some non-urgent care was rescheduled.

known_gaps.text: MDA does not appear in EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json; no baseline source record was available to extend for this ISO.
The NDC and IMF paper do not establish a local climate-to-armed-conflict pathway; NDC child-protection risks are source-stated but are not conflict-incidence estimates.
The full October 2026 Dniester PDNA was not yet posted; incident and response claims rely on the Government's direct summary, and proposed recovery actions were provisional.
The World Bank water-security diagnostic timed out and the 2025 UNDP vulnerable-groups report exceeded the reader limit; neither report's search snippets were used as evidence.
The UNHCR 2025 annual report PDF returned an access/rate-limit error and was not used as evidence.
No directly read source showed armed insecurity interrupting delivery of a named climate-adaptation project in Moldova.
A war-related pollution/service shock is retained as contextual FCV sensitivity, not relabelled as a climate-caused event or a verified blockade of a named adaptation project.
The NDC's child-poverty passage does not itself establish a climate-to-protection causal chain.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
